title: Choose the dashboard's new visual world
question: The roll assigned the Orienteering Course. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Orienteering Course
options.lineage: IOF orienteering maps with the purple course overprint
options.thesis: What to fix first is a course: numbered control circles joined by purple legs across your architecture, read beside a control-description sheet.
materials: map white with open-land yellow and vegetation greens for layers
purple overprint for the course only
options.viewport: Forest-green rail with sections and counts; header with project, analysis status, version, commit and Re-analyze; a legend row of real counts (errors, cycles, layers, vulnerabilities with a Check button); below, the architecture as terrain bands with the purple course 1→4 on the left and the control-description sheet (numbered findings, each opening to its fix) on the right.
options.risk: Orienteering maps are less familiar to developers than transit maps; the course metaphor must stay functional (ranked findings) or it becomes decoration.

raised.raise: Two type sizes for working text; rank carried by weight, case and reversal instead of more sizes, which un-crams dense tables.
Every control carries a stable code (the violation fingerprint), the way each orienteering control has a code.
All neutrals come from one disciplined tonal ramp; no ad-hoc greys.
Focus is total: selecting a control dims everything off its legs and lifts its row.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Layers are colored lines and files are stations; a violation is a line that skips to a station it should never reach.
options.viewport: Black top bar navigation; the layer lines drawn across the work area with stations; a status column of numbered service alerts with fixes.
options.risk: The most familiar direction: transit-map dependency diagrams are where many tools in this category land.

options.label: Dark Developer Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels divided by hairline seams, syntax-derived accents for state only.
options.viewport: Persistent panels: counts strip, where-to-start list, layer stack.
options.case: Developers identify with it instantly; it loses on product clarity because nothing in it shows what to fix first beyond a list.
options.risk: Close to the category default the redesign is meant to leave.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.case: Raked containers fight a working dashboard; developers do not identify with it.
options.kept: A strict type scale where rank is weight and case.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Replacing names with color codes hides the file paths the task depends on.
options.kept: A stable catalog code on every item.

options.label: Exposure Record Sheets
options.case: Overlapping translucent sheets obscure dense findings.
options.kept: One tonal ramp as the only neutrals.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.case: Poster rows have no place for paths, rules and fixes.
options.kept: Total focus: the selected item lifts, everything else dims.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.case: No audience identification; plates do not carry a graph.
options.kept: Comparable views keep one exact scale.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light SaaS dashboard: KPI cards, a findings table, a blue primary action.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, four KPI cards, a where-to-start table and a layers card.
canonCard.risk: Clean and familiar, and indistinguishable from every other dashboard.
